subject: two reference trajectories expressed with the official Opentrons package

overview.what: two reference trajectories used as the golden standard a sandbox agent must reproduce
overview.official_only: reproduction must be done entirely inside the official opentrons package: trajectories are written with the official protocol_api, and grading uses the command sequence produced by the official tools (`opentrons analyze` / `opentrons simulate`). No bespoke host-side script is involved.
overview.reconstruction_note: the original recordings happened mostly at the host-side maintenance-run layer (Protocol Engine commands such as moveToAddressableAreaForDropTip, dropTipInPlace, moveRelative) plus bespoke scripts (a local control console, --override-z, --start/--finish). The two trajectories below are a RECONSTRUCTION of the observed motions as official protocol_api protocols, not a verbatim transcription. The measured constants the reconstruction relies on are listed under inputs.
substitutions_made: the recorded arc-height retry was a host-script policy (start at 150, subtract 20 each attempt, floor 90). The official-API equivalent is to pass a safe minimum_z_height to move_to directly.
the recorded moveToAddressableAreaForDropTip corresponds to the official drop_tip.
dropped_because_no_official_equivalent: run-level labware offset injection (offsets belong to the run layer, not to the protocol)
the fifteen-point human-confirmed check built on waitForResume
overview.why_calibration: physical labware does not match the model: rack width, tube mouth height and plate placement all deviate, e.g. slot 3's peptide rack is about 1% narrower than the model. The deviations are measured once, written into labware offsets applied at the run layer, so the protocol itself contains no offsets.
overview.deck_note: peptide samples live in the tube racks at slots 3/6/7/8; slot 3 is the only slot on a custom labware definition
overview.grading_scope: coordinates and offsets are not what these trajectories test; offsets are applied at the run layer. What they test is how these motions are expressed with the official API.
overview.companion_file: ORIGINAL-RECORDS.md holds the raw real-machine operation records, including the host-side layers and human judgement steps that this reconstruction drops
overview.feedback_channel: T2 requires a per-step observation that the official package does not provide. The sandbox supplies it as a coarse proximity bucket. Agent actions remain entirely official API; only the observation comes from the sandbox.

official_reference.code:
from opentrons import protocol_api

requirements = {"robotType": "OT-2", "apiLevel": "2.16"}

SAFE_TRAVERSE_Z = 130.0   # below the Z limit, so the arc is accepted

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    protocol.load_labware("corning_96_wellplate_360ul_flat", 1)
    tiprack = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 2)
    rack3 = protocol.load_labware_from_definition(SLOT3_DEF, 3)
    protocol.load_labware("opentrons_15_tuberack_falcon_15ml_conical", 4)
    protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 5)
    rack6 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_eppendorf_2ml_safelock_snapcap", 6)
    rack7 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_eppendorf_2ml_safelock_snapcap", 7)
    rack8 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_eppendorf_2ml_safelock_snapcap", 8)

    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "left", tip_racks=[tiprack])

    protocol.home()

    for rack in (rack3, rack7, rack6, rack8):
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        p20.move_to(rack["A1"].top(), minimum_z_height=SAFE_TRAVERSE_Z)
        p20.drop_tip()

grading: all four target slots appear; the order need not be enforced but all four must be present

move_to carries minimum_z_height. This is the core of the trajectory: without it the engine derives the arc apex from deck geometry, which may land at a height the Z limit rejects. The observed runs show that 180 and 150 were each rejected once, so a conservative value is required rather than a fixed number.
force_direct=True is not used anywhere. It would make the tip travel in a straight line through obstacles; the recording never used it and a protocol should not either.
the analysis returns result: ok and errors: 0, with no Arc out of bounds or Destination out of bounds

operations.name: step down gradually to calibrate the aspiration landing point
operations.tests: with the tube bottom unknown, descend in stages using a coarse proximity signal, stop 2 mm above the physical tube bottom; the descent must be staged and must not reach the bottom
operations.scoring: an external scorer, hidden from the agent, judges the stop position and the descent process

inputs.feedback_content: the sandbox returns only the bucket name, never a distance value
inputs.stop_rule: stop on entering 快贴底, which puts the tip end 1 to 2 mm above the physical bottom

official_reference.core_point: all agent actions go through the official API; descending is expressed as well.top(z=-d). probe() is a sandbox-provided observation outside the official package.

grading: stop position: the tip end must be 1 to 3 mm above the physical tube bottom. With the buckets above, stopping on entering 快贴底 lands inside that window.
process: the descent must be staged. No single step above 10 mm, and the step size must not grow once a closer bucket is entered. A single-shot descent, or a step size that grows and shrinks, fails.
no contact: entering 触底风险, or touching the bottom, fails.
operations.design_coupling: the bucket boundaries and the acceptance window are coupled: 1 to 2 mm is its own bucket so that stopping on entry always lands within 1 to 3 mm. Changing the acceptance window requires changing the boundaries, otherwise the task becomes unsolvable or trivial.
operations.basis: ORIGINAL-RECORDS.md 记录二: in the original run the tube bottom was found by staged descent plus visual judgement; here the eye is replaced by the coarse buckets

reading_notes: these two trajectories are reconstructions of host-side recordings into official protocol_api form, not verbatim transcriptions
slot 3's mouth absolute Z is marked as not settled in the parameter file: two visual reads differed by about 54 mm. Here it is used as a given input only.
offsets are applied at the run layer and are deliberately absent from the protocols; the trajectories test how the motions are expressed, not the numbers themselves
